name: UMB Financial Corporation
moat_justification: Moderate regional-bank franchise, high quality for its class: operating ROTCE 20.3% in Q2 2026 with a 48.1% operating efficiency ratio and return on average common equity of 14.16% (Q2 2026 release, via search results), and a filed ROE history (fundamentals.json) of 11.2% / 16.2% / 11.3% / 12.7% in FY2021-FY2024 (FY2025's 9.1% divides by a year-end equity balance swollen by the Heartland stock issuance). fundamentals.json carries no roic_proxy or gross margin for a bank presentation (both null), so ROE/ROTCE are the return evidence. Capped at moderate because the core product is commodity banking with no structural pricing power (NIM 3.32% FTE in Q2 2026 is earned through the cycle, not owned), the enlarged loan book is untested through a credit cycle, and growth/returns now depend on holding Heartland's deposits and delivering synergies after the October 2025 conversion. A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
DILUTION: share count growing 14.8%/yr — already deducted via the growth adjustment; check SBC trend
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2024 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base

CAPEX_COVERAGE_LOW: capex is below 50% of D&A in each of the last 3 fiscal years (FY2023 39%, FY2024 38%, FY2025 34%) at a filer with positive PP&E — reconcile total capex against the cash-flow statement's investing section (construction in progress, capitalised software, land-use rights, spectrum, intangible purchases) before trusting the owner's-earnings base
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Finance sector — OE/capex DCF fits finance names poorly; grade confidence low
BASE_DIVERGENCE: latest FY OE/share 12.76 vs 3-yr median 8.83 — one of them is distorted; find out which and why
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.5x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
BIG_NET_CASH: net cash is 7.6x normalized OE — part of the price is a cash pile, not the operating business; note it in the verdict
TIER_BAND: bear-case tier C (10.1%) vs bull-case tier B (18.3%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: High-quality regional bank (institutional fee franchise, 48% efficiency, operating ROTCE 20.3%), moat 5/10 — on the clean post-Heartland TTM base of $13.10/sh the weighted IRR is 14.43% (IV@15% $123.46 vs $129.65), Tier C by numbers and softened to D under the universal bank-misfit notch; it clears 15% only below ~$123; confidence low.
tier_override_reason: SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH universal softening (Andrew's standing rule 2026-10-15, made universal 2026-10-19): a bank's OCF-based OE is not distributable earnings — loan growth consumes regulatory capital and the provision is a through-cycle cost OCF adds back ($154,500,000 in FY2025, Form 10-K cash-flow reconciliation), while FY2025 earnings also carry $139,775,000 of net purchase-accounting accretion from Heartland. The numbers tier C (weighted IRR 14.43%) already sits below the hurdle, and the identical scenario set on the filing-clean median base prints a weighted IRR of 10.67% (IV@15% $83.28) — the TTM print is the top of the defensible range, taken in a benign credit window (Q2 2026 net charge-offs 16bp). Softened one notch to D, confidence low.
moat_for: Institutional Banking fee franchise — fund administration/accounting, custody and HSA/healthcare payment services are sticky, fee-rich and less capital-intensive than lending; noninterest income was $245.5M in Q2 2026, +10.5% YoY (Q2 2026 release)
Deposit franchise at scale — deposits $59.8B at June 30, 2026 against loans of $41.2B (a conservative loan-to-deposit posture), funding the balance sheet cheaply enough for a 3.32% FTE NIM
Best-in-class efficiency for a regional — operating efficiency ratio 48.14% in Q2 2026 (GAAP 48.35%), well ahead of large-regional peers, with operating ROTCE of 20.3% in the quarter
Asset quality and underwriting record — net charge-offs 16bp of average loans and nonperforming loans 31bp of total loans in Q2 2026; OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years

Heartland step-up delivered so far — acquisition closed January 31, 2025, systems/brand conversion completed October 2025, and Q2 2026 operating EPS of $3.57 was +21.1% YoY on a clean combined-vs-combined comparison
moat_against: Commodity product, no structural pricing power — deposits and loans are fungible; NIM and deposit pricing are set by money-center banks, regionals and money-market alternatives

Credit-cycle exposure on an enlarged, unseasoned book — loans $41.2B at June 30, 2026 after the Heartland step-up, assembled in a benign stretch (charge-offs 16bp are a trough print, not a through-cycle level); FY2025 provision for credit losses was $154.5M even in a good year

Purchase-accounting accretion is a fading tailwind inside current earnings — the FY2025 cash-flow reconciliation shows net accretion of premiums/discounts from acquisition of $139,775,000 boosting FY2025 results
Capital-constrained growth — loan growth, the raised $0.50 quarterly dividend (+16.3%, declared for October 1, 2026) and any buybacks compete for the same regulatory capital

Rate sensitivity — earnings lean on NIM (net interest income $532.5M in Q2 2026, +14.0% YoY) and on lumpy private-investment gains ($27.1M in Q2 2026, including SpaceX-related fund gains, per the release)
